fields.Q1:
WHAT IS STANDING AROUND THIS ROOM MADE OF?**
Cut stone laid in courses — flat rectangular blocks with thin recessed joints. But that is a guess from silhouette, not from surface. At the size shown I could not tell you what it would feel like: there is no grain, no tooling, no chip, no pitting, no colour of its own. It is grey where it is unlit and brown where light reaches it, and that is all the information the material gives.
fields.Q1_WHY: Magnifying the north band at x=55–725, y=232–252 (stretched 8× vertically at `/tmp/nwall_L.png`) shows every block is a **single flat fill** — one uniform value per rectangle, bounded by a 1–2 px darker joint. Nothing inside them. Compare the field beyond the wall at x=250–370, y=0–228: same thing, larger — 8 px dark bands separated by ~24 px flat fills, edges detected at y=23/31, 53/61, 87/95, 117/125. Regular flat courses, zero interior information. The blocks are shapes, not surfaces.
fields.Q2:
SOLID MASS, OR A FLAT PATTERN AROUND THE EDGE?**
**A flat pattern.** Not close.

The determining measurement: at y=225, the "solid wall" column at x=300 reads luminance 18. The open passage floor at x=405, same row, also reads 18. Identical. The renderer draws mass and void at the same brightness and the same visual height; the only difference between them is which texture got stamped there.

Supporting: the north boundary is 2–3 px of near-black (y=230–232, luminance 14.9→4.3) followed by a ~20 px band of blocks, against a 64 px grid cell. No side face, no cap, no bevel, no occlusion, no cast shadow onto the floor. The west boundary at x=55 is worse — a **1–2 px seam** (luminance 9.7 at x=54, 5.6 at x=56) with nothing on either side of it. Two pixels of darker colour is the entire west wall.
fields.Q3:
WHERE EXACTLY DOES THE GROUND STOP?**
Three different answers on three sides, which is itself the problem.

- **North, y≈230:** 2 px of (2,2,2) black, then a 20 px band of flat blocks (y=234–252, sampled at x=600: 9,9,9,9,3,5,6,7), then floor. Transition ≈22 px.
- **West, x≈55:** 2 px. Floor at x=54 is (7,7,9); x=55–56 is (3,3,3); x=60 is (4,4,6). A colour change, nothing more.
- **South, y≈772:** the map is simply **cut by the viewport** — luminance falls 9.2→3.2 across y=760–772, then jumps to the flat app-chrome grey (11,11,14) at y=774. There is no south wall. The room ends because the screen does.
- **East:** no seam exists. I scanned every column x=700–749; the values sit flat at 6–7 with no discontinuity. The floor runs off the right edge of the frame.
fields.Q4:
WHAT IS HOLDING THIS PLACE TOGETHER?**
**NOTHING.** Nothing in this image is visibly bearing, bracing, tying or carrying anything.

There are two candidate objects and both fail. At x=130–148, y=190–227 there is a vertical post with three crossbars — a stake or rack — and at x=565–571, y=190–227 a plain 6 px vertical bar. Both sit *on* the northern wall field, both are flat 2–3 colour fills, both cast no shadow, and neither touches or spans anything. For a place held for four hundred years by people who repair with rope, driven pins and salvaged timber, there is not one rope, one pin, one plank, one bracket or one patch anywhere on the standing structure.
fields.Q5:
BUILT, OR AN IMAGE THAT WAS REPEATED?**
**Repeated.** The wall field's courses come at a metronome: edge-detection down the west field (x=5–50) gives y=279/287, 309/317, 343/351, 373/381, 407/415 — 30, 34, 30, 34. The north field (x=250–370) gives 23, 53, 87, 117 — 30, 34, 30. Two unrelated regions of the map, 300 px apart, running the identical 32 px cadence with the identical 8 px band, unbroken for 500 px. Nothing bonds at a corner, nothing changes at a junction, nothing steps or thickens where load would go.
fields.Q6:
WOULD YOU BELIEVE THIS SHIPPED IN A COMMERCIAL GAME?**
**YES** — the lighting falloff is convincing and the silhouette reads.

Merely competent, or genuinely good? **Merely competent, and only on the ground plane.** The standing structure is not competent. A wall you cannot distinguish from an open corridor by brightness, that is two pixels thick on one side and absent on two others, is a placeholder that has been lit well.
fields.Q7:
WHAT CAN YOU ACTUALLY SEE AT 1:1?**
On the standing surfaces: **almost nothing, and past ~150 px from the figure, nothing at all.**

- x=380–560, y=232–252 (the lit stretch of the north band): at 1:1 I can see *that it is banded* — a dark line and one or two lighter courses. I cannot see an individual block edge. Native crop at `/tmp/native_gap1x.png` is a brown smear.
- x=55–300 and x=600–725, same rows: **blank.** A dark strip. No block divisions legible whatsoever.
- x=0–54 (the whole west wall): **blank at 1:1.** I did not know there was a course pattern there until I lifted the gamma by 4.5 stops.
- x=240–570, y=0–228 (beyond the north wall): **blank.** Reads as fog.

Yes, it changes with distance — but the fall is a cliff, not a slope, and it lands at *zero information* rather than at *simplified information*. Everything I reported in Q1 and Q5 was hunted for at 4–8× with heavy gamma lift. None of it is seeing.
fields.Q7_WHY: Checked at 1:1, unmodified: x=300–560/y=215–290; x=0–120/y=220–540; x=600–750/y=220–340; x=240–570/y=0–245. Required magnification (4–8×, gamma 0.22–0.35): the block courses in the north band, the entire west course pattern, both posts at x=130 and x=565, and the course-spacing regularity.
fields.Q8:
ANYTHING YOUR EYE KEEPS RETURNING TO?**
Three things.

1. **The two black rectangles**, x=0–246/y=0–140 and x=568–750/y=0–140. Hard-edged: (1,1,2) at x=246, (9,9,12) at x=248 — a 2 px step. They are perfectly axis-aligned and they **clip the wall courses mid-band** with a razor edge. Nothing in a stone room produces a rectangular hole in vision. Your eye goes there because it is the only high-contrast edge in the upper half of the frame, and it is a UI artifact.
2. **The 32 px course rhythm**, at the same phase everywhere it appears (Q5 measurements). Once seen it does not stop being seen.
3. **The panel at x=183–248, y=455–518.** A one-cell object with a pale flat top and two courses beneath, sitting unattached in open floor. At (215,470) it reads (100,73,49); floor at the *same radius from the light* on the other side, (595,470), reads (74,54,37). It is 35% too bright for its distance. It is not lit — it is pasted.
fields.Q9:
WHAT IS BEYOND THE WALLS?**
**More of the same stuff, unlit.** Not void, not another room, not unknowable — the same courses as the wall itself, continuing without interruption to the frame edge (x=240–570, y=0–228, and the entire west field x=0–54, y=232–770). The 32 px cadence runs straight through where a wall's far face ought to be. Nothing terminates. Nothing implies a space on the other side.

The two black rectangles are the only "unknown", and they are unknown because a rectangle was drawn over them, not because anything in the world occludes them. This is the biggest miss against the fiction: an administered underworld in continuous heavy use, and beyond its walls there is neither another cell of the filing system nor darkness with weight — just the same wallpaper, dimmed.
fields.Q10:
COULD YOU TELL A WAY THROUGH FROM A DEAD END?**
**Yes — and it is the one thing in this image that works.**

The gap is at x≈378–438 (≈62 px, one grid cell), running north from y=232 off the top of the frame. I read it as **a passage**, confidently, before measuring.

What made the difference was not the gap in the wall — it was that the channel carries **floor texture and floor damage**: irregular slabs and two long hairline cracks running diagonally through it at y≈95–160 and y≈245–290. The flanking wall field carries neither. Profiling up the corridor (x=405: y=225→18, 210→13, 180→10, 120→6) versus up the wall (x=300: 225→18, 210→15, 180→8, 120→8) shows the light *travels* up the corridor and stalls on the wall. That gradient is the read.

Worth naming plainly: the passage is legible because of the ground plane and the lighting, both of which are out of scope here. The standing structure contributes nothing to it — the wall does not thicken, return, jamb or shadow at the opening. Remove the floor texture and the corridor disappears.
fields.Q11:
HAS ANYTHING HAPPENED TO THIS STRUCTURE?**
**No. Nothing has happened to it.**

The floor is cracked in at least four places I can trace. The standing structure carries **zero** damage marks — no spall, no missing block, no slumped course, no soot, no staining, no patch, no repair. Every course edge I detected (y=279/287/309/317/343/351/373/381/407/415 west; y=23/31/53/61/87/95/117/125 north) is straight and on-pitch. Not one block is out of line.

I read that from the contradiction: the same artist put cracks in the ground and none on the walls. This structure is either brand new or was never used, and the fiction says it has been in continuous heavy use since before records began, held by a company that has been repairing it for four hundred years. The walls do not know that.
fields.CULL: Walls are a flat texture swap, not mass — at y=225 wall and open passage read identical brightness.
fields.FLIP LIST:
- Give the wall real thickness: at minimum one full 64 px cell of dark mass on the north and west edges, with a visible inner face and a 6–10 px contact shadow cast onto the floor along y≈252 and x≈57–70.
- Kill the 32 px metronome. Break the course cadence at least every 3–4 cells — a dropped block, a shifted joint, a course that runs out — across x=0–54 and x=240–570.
- Put four hundred years of orc repair on the standing surfaces where the light reaches: driven pins, a lashed timber spanning a broken course, hide over a gap. Concentrate it at x=380–560, y=232–252, where the player can actually see it at 1:1.
- Replace the two hard black rectangles (x=0–246 and x=568–750, y=0–140) with a soft, non-rectangular occlusion so the wall stops being clipped mid-course by a UI shape.
- Fix the unlit panel at x=183–248, y=455–518 — it reads 35% brighter than floor at the same radius from the figure, and it attaches to nothing.
